decision_authority.policy: MRX continuous quality-gated publication and two-image article creative directive

title: Understanding Mineral Rights for New Owners
findings: Complete current MDX SHA-256 is 7daa4944534a0349b2de103eb8d0970c99ca6bcbd14682fed0d8a4b2d215a588; all 8 declared sources passed live access review.

MRX claims remain bounded to its current methodology and FAQ; ownership-orientation claims remain bounded to Railroad Commission and General Land Office explanations; operational-data claims preserve Railroad Commission reporting scope and limitations; and the unclaimed-property note remains bounded to the Comptroller search resource.

The article uses no fabricated owners, buyers, contracts, deeds, prices, acreage, ownership decimals, tax results, offers, testimonials, success rates, or owner-specific title, legal, tax, accounting, appraisal, investment, or transaction conclusions.

sources_inspected.label: Mineral Rights Xchange, Published DCF Methodology (accessed 2026-08-12)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The current MRX methodology describes a directional DCF range with dated inputs, assumptions, limitations, and sensitivity, and separates asset range from offer consideration and expected owner net.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses the methodology only for the disclosed directional framework, input-status discipline, sensitivity review, and transaction separation; it does not value a specific interest, establish ownership, or recommend a transaction.

sources_inspected.label: Mineral Rights Xchange, Frequently Asked Questions (accessed 2026-08-12)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The current MRX FAQ describes the review as educational, directional, and not certified, and states that a possible later MRX buyer relationship is disclosed when applicable.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses the FAQ only for the professional boundary and potential economic-interest disclosure; it does not promise value, price, an offer, payment, or closing.

sources_inspected.label: Railroad Commission of Texas, Oil and Gas Exploration and Surface Ownership (accessed 2026-08-12)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The Railroad Commission of Texas explains that surface and mineral estates may be owned together or severed and states that the page provides general information rather than legal advice.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses the page only to flag the surface/mineral distinction for a new-owner record; it does not interpret dominance, accommodation, access, a deed, a reservation, or an owner-specific legal result.

sources_inspected.label: Railroad Commission of Texas, Royalties FAQ (accessed 2026-08-12)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The Railroad Commission of Texas identifies public production and permit resources, payment-detail fields, payor-change information, division-order and owner-request categories, and its limited role in private lease and royalty matters.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses the page only to organize identifiers, payor records, check detail, and follow-up questions; it does not decide payment entitlement, lease meaning, title, statutory compliance, or a dispute.

sources_inspected.label: Railroad Commission of Texas, Online Research Queries (accessed 2026-08-12)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The Railroad Commission of Texas provides public research-query surfaces for Texas production, drilling permits, well records, operators, fields, and related oil-and-gas information.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses these queries only for dated operational context and identifiers; it does not treat a query result as proof of ownership, tract inclusion, payment entitlement, reserves, future development, or value.

sources_inspected.label: Railroad Commission of Texas, Production Data Query System FAQs (accessed 2026-08-12)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The Railroad Commission of Texas explains the lease-level reporting scope of Texas oil production, gas-lease reporting, the production-data lag, revisions, and historical completeness limitations.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses the page only to preserve the reporting unit, date, lag, and revision status; it does not allocate lease production to a tract, well, owner, decimal, or payment.

sources_inspected.label: Texas General Land Office, Minerals FAQ (accessed 2026-08-12)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The Texas General Land Office minerals FAQ distinguishes original-grant records held by the GLO from later county deed records and warns that descent from an original grantee does not itself establish mineral ownership.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses the FAQ only to route original-grant and later county-record research; it does not determine a title chain, inheritance, reservation, conveyance, or ownership result.

sources_inspected.label: Texas Comptroller, Unclaimed Property (accessed 2026-08-12)
sources_inspected.source_location_or_paraphrase: The Texas Comptroller lists mineral interests among unclaimed-property types and directs users to the state claim-search resource.
sources_inspected.claim_scope: The article uses the page only to identify a possible search and verification step; it does not establish ownership, entitlement, payment, tax treatment, or claim approval.
